content_md:
# Blygger Studio 0.8.3 shipped 

There may be bugs.

## Four releases in a day: what changed in Blygger Studio

`blygger-studio` went 0.7.0 → 0.8.3 today, across four releases. Both my nodes
are on 0.8.3. Here is what you can actually see, and the one thing you have to
do if you are upgrading.

**If you are on 0.7.0 or earlier, this is not a bare deploy.** 0.8.0 carries
migration `0012`. Apply migrations, then deploy. The backfill is written so that
upgrading changes nothing currently visible on your pages — existing opt-ins
become hard overrides and everything else inherits a default that is off.

## Quoting part of something (0.8.1)

The medium had three registers of borrowing and only two were writable:
transclude an item whole, or fork from a pin. Quoting a passage — the ordinary
blogging move — was the missing rung.

A directive followed immediately, with no blank line, by a blockquote is now a
**partial transclusion**:


Commentary begins after a blank line.


A blank line detaches it, so "transclude the whole thing, then quote a bit of it
myself" — legal since 0.1 — still means what it always did. Nothing anyone has
already written changes.

The passage has to actually be in the target at the version being baked, or the
publish fails like an unresolvable directive. A quote that welds two of the
source's paragraphs into one sentence is refused, because the source has a break
there and the quote does not.

In the studio: **highlight a passage in the reading view and press `quote ↗`**.
You land in the editor with the directive and the passage already attached, and
it is checked while you are still choosing it rather than at publish. Stubbing a
long item prefills an empty quote line instead of the whole thing — delete the
line and you get the old behaviour.

On the page a partial quote says **"excerpt of v2"** where a whole one says
"snapshot of v2". Without that you cannot tell a part from the whole: a short
quote and a short item look identical.

On the wire it is an optional `selector` on the `transclusions[]` entry, W3C
text-quote shape. **A reader that ignores it entirely stays conformant** — the
passage is baked into `content_html` like any transclusion, the relation is
still `transclusion`, staleness is unchanged, and mention verification ignores
it. Still protocol 0.3; this is a revision, not a new version.

## Thread cards stopped putting words in my mouth (0.8.2)

A thread's stored HTML contains other people's writing, baked in as quotes. That
is correct on the thread's own page, where a quote is shown as a quote with
provenance under it. It was wrong everywhere the client had to *name* the thread
in one line.

Of my 19 published threads, **five opened with a transclusion** — which is the
shape the stub action prefills, so it is the common case, not an edge one. For
those five, the browser tab, the search-result heading, the social card, the RSS
headline and the feed-page excerpt were all somebody else's sentence presented
as mine. Others ran my prose straight into a quote mid-excerpt, so a card read
as one continuous paragraph by one person when it was two.

Fixed in one place and used by all four surfaces. Cards also carry a **`⧉2`
quote count** now, which is what says the item is longer than the teaser. A
thread that quotes without adding anything of its own names what it answers
instead of borrowing the quoted sentence.

Nothing on the wire changed: the item document, the feed and the static export
all keep the quotes.

## Your blyg stops being called "blyg" (0.8.3)

The default title was the literal string `blyg`, so everyone who skipped that
settings field published under the same name. Two unrelated live blygs were
doing exactly that.

It now derives from your own address — a blyg at `blyg.example.com` titles
itself `example.com` until you say otherwise. Your own title always wins.
Deliberately not a made-up human name: "Example's Blyg" would be the software
asserting something you never said.

There is an advisory for other client authors at
[blygger.org/start/](https://blygger.org/start/) — the general form is that a
default identical across installations destroys information, and the deployment
usually already knows a truer answer. **Name collisions themselves are fine.**
Two people may both call their blyg "Joe's blyg"; the domain tells them apart.

`npm run upgrade` also moves between **releases** now rather than to the tip of
`main`, so it and the update notice finally agree about what "current" means.

## Studio chrome (0.8.0)

- **The nav is a real top menu** — tabs with a current state, utilities in their
  own group, collapsing behind a hamburger below 640px.
- **A mobile pass over every studio and public page.** One pasted URL used to
  set the page's minimum width, so *every* page scrolled sideways; tap targets
  were 18–26px where they needed to be ~44; the reading sidebar pushed the
  stream off the first screen and now collapses behind a control that names the
  source you are filtered to.
- **Shared links unfurl properly.** A titled item's card is its title and then
  its body, rather than the title followed by the title again as the opening
  words. Pinned pages and the archive carry an image. The archive listing shows
  a title and a separate excerpt instead of running them together.
